descripcion_es: Regular and irregular verbs; the auxiliary did in questions and negatives.
resumen: The past simple expresses actions finished at a specific moment in the past (yesterday, last year, in 2010, ago). It almost always corresponds to the Spanish pretérito indefinido.

explicacion.texto: In the affirmative, regular verbs add -ed (work → worked; if they end in -e, just -d: live → lived). Irregular verbs have their own form, which you have to memorise (go → went, see → saw, buy → bought). The form is the same for all persons.

filas: subject + past form of the verb
Yes, subject + did / No, subject + didn't
Yes, she did. / No, she didn't.

explicacion.texto: With did / didn't the main verb goes back to the infinitive: the auxiliary already marks the past. That's why “Did you went?” and “I didn't saw” are wrong.

items: Spelling: stop → stopped (final consonant doubled after a short stressed vowel), study → studied (consonant + y → -ied), play → played (vowel + y → -ed).
Pronunciation of -ed: /t/ after voiceless sounds (worked), /d/ after voiced sounds (played), /ɪd/ after t or d (wanted, needed).
The verb be doesn't use did: was / were, wasn't / weren't, Was he...?

filas: to move to a place (es: ir)
to pick up, to use (es: tomar, coger)
to obtain, to arrive (es: conseguir, llegar)
to put words on paper (es: escribir)
to go away, to let stay (es: salir, dejar)

explicacion.texto: Typical time markers: yesterday, last night / week / year, two days ago, in 1998, when I was a child.

ejemplos.frase: We watched a film last night.
I bought these shoes two weeks ago.
ejemplos.traduccion: Compré estos zapatos hace dos semanas.

ejemplos.frase: Did you call your mother yesterday?
He didn't come to the party.

ejemplos.traduccion: El tren salió a las siete.

errores_hispanohablantes.nota: After did, the verb is in the infinitive.
The negative with didn't also takes the infinitive.
With yesterday, ago or a past date we use the past simple, not the present perfect.
The verb be forms questions without did.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the verb in the past simple.
ejercicios.explicacion: The rule for regular verbs applies: they add -ed in the affirmative. The clue is last summer, a marker of finished past time that requires the past simple. Travel is regular; in British English it doubles the l (travelled) and in American English it doesn't (traveled), so both forms are accepted. The form is the same with we as with any other person.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Regular verb: travel + -ed (travelled in British English, traveled in American English).
ejercicios.traduccion: Viajamos a Portugal el verano pasado.

errores_previstos.explicacion: With last summer, a finished past time, we don't use the present perfect but the past simple.
The past ending -ed is missing.
The -ing form on its own is not a tense; the past simple is travelled (or traveled).

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the verb in the past simple.
ejercicios.frase: She ___ (write) a long letter to her grandmother.
ejercicios.explicacion: The rule for irregular verbs applies: they have their own past form; write appears in the table of irregular verbs in the unit: write → wrote. The clue is the instruction, which asks for the past simple, and the context of a finished event. Be careful not to confuse the past wrote with the past participle written.
ejercicios.traduccion: Escribió una carta larga a su abuela.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Write is irregular: its past is wrote; you don't add -ed.
Written is the past participle; the past simple is wrote.
The instruction asks for the past simple, not the present perfect.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the verb in the past simple.
ejercicios.frase: The children ___ (stop) playing when it started to rain.
ejercicios.explicacion: The spelling rule from Rules and key points applies: one-syllable verbs ending in a consonant after a short stressed vowel double the consonant: stop → stopped. The clue is when it started to rain, which places the action in the past. Stop followed by -ing means “to no longer do something”.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Stop doubles the p before -ed: stopped.
ejercicios.traduccion: Los niños dejaron de jugar cuando empezó a llover.

errores_previstos.explicacion: The p must be doubled: stopped. Without doubling, it would be read with a long vowel.
The past ending is missing: stopped.
The instruction asks for the past simple; also, stopping playing is a single, completed action.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the negative form of the past simple.
ejercicios.explicacion: The “Negative” row of the table applies: subject + didn't + infinitive. The clue is last night, finished past time, and the instruction to use the negative. Didn't marks the past, so sleep goes back to the infinitive; that's why you don't write slept. Both the contraction and the full form are accepted.

errores_previstos.explicacion: After didn't the verb is in the infinitive: sleep. The auxiliary already marks the past.
In English you don't make a negative by putting not before the verb; you need the auxiliary didn't.
Don't is present; with last night you need didn't.

ejercicios.explicacion: The rule for the verb be in the past applies; it has two forms: was for I, he, she, it and were for you, we, they and plural nouns. The clue is the shops, a plural subject, which requires were. Be never uses did.
ejercicios.traduccion: Las tiendas estaban cerradas el domingo.

errores_previstos.explicacion: The shops is plural: were.
Here closed is an adjective after be; you need the verb be (were), not the auxiliary did.

ejercicios.explicacion: The “Question” row of the table applies: Did + subject + infinitive, valid for any verb except be. The clue is enjoy, a main verb in the infinitive after the subject, and the context of a concert that is already over. That's why Did. Enjoy means to get pleasure from something, and here Spanish would naturally say “gustar”.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: A past question with a verb other than be: Did + subject + infinitive.

por_opcion.Did: Correct: the past auxiliary for questions with verbs other than be.
por_opcion.Were: Incorrect: were only forms questions with be or with continuous forms (Were you enjoying…?), not with an infinitive.
por_opcion.Do: Incorrect: do is present; it would ask whether you usually enjoy the concert, and the concert is already over.

ejercicios.frase: My brother ___ his keys at the office yesterday.
ejercicios.explicacion: The rule for irregular verbs (leave → left, in the table in the unit) and the rule for time markers apply. The clue is yesterday, which requires the past simple. Leave means “to let something stay” or “to forget something somewhere”, and its past is left.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Leave is irregular (left) and yesterday requires the past simple.
ejercicios.traduccion: Mi hermano se dejó las llaves en la oficina ayer.

por_opcion.leaved: Incorrect: leave is irregular; leaved doesn't exist.
por_opcion.left: Correct: the irregular past of leave, suitable with yesterday.
por_opcion.has left: Incorrect: the present perfect is not used with yesterday or with other markers of finished past time.

ejercicios.explicacion: The rule from Rules and key points applies: with did / didn't the main verb goes back to the infinitive, because the auxiliary already marks the past. The clue is didn't just before the gap. That's why know, not its past knew.

por_opcion.knew: Incorrect: after didn't you don't repeat the past; it is the typical mistake “I didn't saw”.
por_opcion.knowed: Incorrect: know is irregular (knew), and anyway after didn't comes the infinitive.

ejercicios.enunciado: Make the sentence negative (use the contraction).
respuestas: He didn't buy a new car.
ejercicios.explicacion: The “Negative” row of the table applies: subject + didn't + infinitive. The clue is bought, the irregular past of buy. When you add didn't, the verb goes back to the infinitive: buy. The instruction asks for the contraction, so didn't.
ejercicios.traduccion: No se compró un coche nuevo.

errores_previstos.respuesta: He didn't bought a new car.
errores_previstos.explicacion: After didn't the verb is in the infinitive: buy.

errores_previstos.respuesta: He doesn't buy a new car.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Doesn't is present; to make a past sentence negative we use didn't.

errores_previstos.respuesta: He not bought a new car.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The negative needs the auxiliary didn't.

ejercicios.enunciado: Turn the sentence into a question.
ejercicios.explicacion: The “Question” row of the table applies: Did + subject + infinitive. The clue is arrived, a regular verb in the past. In the question did carries the past and arrive goes back to the infinitive. The order is Did + they + arrive + late.

errores_previstos.explicacion: After did the verb is in the infinitive: arrive.
A calque of the Spanish question formed by intonation; the written question needs did.
Modern English doesn't invert the main verb; it uses the auxiliary did.

ejercicios.frase: Did you went to the cinema?
respuestas: Did you go to the cinema?
ejercicios.explicacion: The rule that after did the verb goes back to the infinitive applies, together with the first typical mistake in the unit (Did you saw…?). The clue is Did at the beginning, which already marks the past. Went is the past of go and must be changed to go.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: After did, the verb is in the infinitive: go.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Did you went to the cinema?
errores_previstos.explicacion: That is copying the sentence without correcting it: after did the verb is in the infinitive.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Did you gone to the cinema?
errores_previstos.explicacion: Gone is the past participle; after did comes the infinitive go.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Do you go to the cinema?
errores_previstos.explicacion: It changes the tense to present; the original question is in the past.

ejercicios.frase: I have met her three years ago.
respuestas: I met her three years ago.
ejercicios.explicacion: The rule for past time markers applies, together with the third typical mistake in the unit: with ago we use the past simple, not the present perfect. The clue is three years ago, a specific, finished moment in the past. That's why met, the irregular past of meet (“to see someone for the first time”).
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: With ago we use the past simple.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I have met her three years ago.
errores_previstos.explicacion: That is copying the sentence without correcting it: ago doesn't allow the present perfect.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I meet her three years ago.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Meet is present; you need the past met.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I have known her three years ago.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It is still the present perfect with ago; it also changes the meaning.

ejercicios.explicacion: The spelling rule in the unit applies: consonant + y changes to -ied (study → studied). The clue is that study ends in d + y, that is, a consonant plus y. If the y came after a vowel (play), you would just add -ed.

errores_previstos.explicacion: That is copying the sentence without correcting it: consonant + y becomes -ied.
The y doesn't disappear: it changes to i and you add -ed, studied.

errores_previstos.respuesta: She has studied medicine in Salamanca.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It corrects the spelling but changes the tense for no reason; the mistake was only in the spelling.

ejercicios.enunciado: Put the words in order to make a question.
respuestas: Where did you go on holiday
ejercicios.explicacion: The “Question” row of the table applies, with a question word: where + did + subject + infinitive. The clue is where and did among the words. Go is in the infinitive because did already marks the past. On holiday is the British expression for being away from work or school on a trip (es: de vacaciones).

errores_previstos.respuesta: where you did go on holiday
errores_previstos.explicacion: Did goes before the subject in a direct question.

errores_previstos.respuesta: where did you go holiday on
errores_previstos.explicacion: The preposition forms a unit with its noun: on holiday.

respuestas: We missed the bus this morning
This morning we missed the bus
ejercicios.explicacion: The “Affirmative” row of the table applies: subject + past form of the verb. The clue is missed, the regular past of miss (to fail to catch a bus, train, etc.), and this morning, a time marker. The order is subject + verb + object + time expression; the time expression can also go at the beginning.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Subject + past verb + object + time expression.

errores_previstos.respuesta: this morning missed we the bus
errores_previstos.explicacion: The subject goes before the verb even if the sentence begins with the time expression.

errores_previstos.respuesta: we missed this morning the bus
errores_previstos.explicacion: The time expression cannot separate the verb from its direct object.

descripcion_larga_es: The past simple is the basic tense for telling about events finished at a specific moment in the past (yesterday, last year, in 2010, ago), and it almost always corresponds to the Spanish pretérito indefinido. It requires memorising irregular verbs and mastering the auxiliary did in negatives and questions. Spanish speakers find it hardest to go back to the infinitive after did and to avoid the present perfect with past time markers.

contexto.que_es: It is the tense that expresses actions completed at a specific moment in the past. Regular verbs add -ed, irregular verbs have their own form, and the form is the same for all persons. Negatives and questions use the auxiliary did / didn't with the verb in the infinitive, except with the verb be.
contexto.por_que_importa: It is the most common tense for telling stories and talking about your own life, so it comes up in every conversation and every exam. Mistakes with did (Did you went?) and with irregular verbs are very noticeable and suggest a low level. Also, using the present perfect with yesterday or ago is one of the most typical mistakes of Spanish speakers.
contexto.cuando_se_usa: With markers of finished past time: yesterday, last night, last week, two days ago, in 1998, when I was a child. Also for telling a sequence of actions in a story. Spanish speakers, influenced by the Spanish pretérito perfecto (“he visto hoy”, “lo he conocido hace años” in some regions), tend to use have + past participle where English requires the past simple.
